Priya Patel: :warning: Found an old SealedSecrets private key file in a public fork of our infra repo (archived helm charts). File path: infra/helm-charts-archive/sealed-secrets/keys/priv.pem. Fingerprint: SEAL-2022-0a7c. Possible exposure window ~2022-11.

Sam Lee: Oof. Which clusters used that key? any customer namespaces?

Priya Patel: Quick grep across clusters: sealedsecrets in prod, staging, and two dedicated-customer namespaces are signed with SEAL-2022-0a7c. Looks like the helm chart was exported during a migration; artifacts were copied to a public fork accidentally.

Jenna Carter: Threat model: anyone with priv.pem can decrypt SealedSecret objects created with that pub key. We should treat as compromised. Proposed immediate steps:
1) Create incident INC-2026-011 and set severity P2.
2) Generate new keypair isolated, publish new cert, re-seal secrets (staging/dev first), then rotate prod in a maintenance window.
3) Wrap controller private key in KMS (cloud KMS/HSM) to avoid plaintext on disk going forward.
4) Enforce RBAC and audit so only infra/ops SAs can create sealedsecrets and all unwraps/reads are logged.

Marco Rivera: +1. Also block create/patch for sealedsecrets by default and whitelist infra-svcaccount and ops group. Add kube-audit rule to log create/get/delete for secrets & sealedsecrets and push to central logging.

Priya Patel: Timeline suggestion (short):
- T+0: declare incident, notify CISO/legal.
- T+1h: stand up new ed25519 key on isolated admin host, upload public cert to internal secure bucket (restricted to infra-admins).
- T+2-4h: run re-seal job in dev/staging, verify app behavior.
- T+8-12h: rotate in prod during agreed window, run post-rotation audits for 72h.

Sam Lee: Re-seal steps I ran in dev (commands):
```
# generate new key
openssl genpkey -algorithm ed25519 -out sealed-new.key
openssl pkey -in sealed-new.key -pubout -out sealed-new.pub
# create kubeseal cert (controller expects tls.crt style)
kubeseal --cert sealed-new.pub < secret.yaml > sealedsecret.yaml
kubectl apply -f sealedsecret.yaml
```
Note: for prod we'll use KMS-wrapped key and helm values to point controller at unwrap config.

Jenna Carter: I'll draft the KMS-wrapping helm values and chart changes. Controller will fetch wrapped key from KMS on startup (IAM role with decrypt permission). We'll create Vault audit sinks to capture unwrap/decrypt calls.

Marco Rivera: RBAC PR coming. Will restrict the sealedsecrets CRD verbs to namespace-level infra-svcaccount and ops group via a ClusterRole/RoleBinding pattern. Also will add an admission check to reject sealedsecret creation unless keyFingerprint annotation present and matches current active key. That helps detect old-key sealed objects.

Priya Patel: Operational runbook notes (to be attached to INC-2026-011):
- Enumerate SealedSecret objects using `kubectl get sealedsecret --all-namespaces -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.namespace} {.metadata.name} {.metadata.annotations.sealedsecrets.bitnami.com/keyFingerprint}\n{end}' | grep SEAL-2022-0a7c`
- For each hit: ops only — export plaintext from secret store (Vault or K8s secret) with least privilege, re-seal with new cert, apply, and verify pod rollout.
- Remove old private key from any cluster secrets and from archived storage; rotate any KMS keys if evidence shows they were exported.

Sam Lee: Automation notes: I wrote a re-seal job that preserves labels/annotations used by apps, patches ownerReferences, and runs a canary rollout. It also records a mapping CSV: old-ns,old-name -> new-sealed-name and includes the keyFingerprint annotation.

Jenna Carter: Scheduling: I'll reserve 18:00 UTC for prod rotation. Oncall: @sam.lee will execute; Marco to merge RBAC PR earlier in the day.

sec-bot: INC-2026-011 created by priya.patel. Severity: P2. Incident channel: #inc-2026-011

deploy-bot: deploy queued: infra/rbac-lockdown PR#789 -> staging. CI: passed. Link: https://ci.internal/build/789

Priya Patel: Additional detection: run grep across CI artifacts `grep -R "SEAL-2022-0a7c" /tmp/gh-archive || true` and GH forks index. If we find other leaks, add to incident page and rotate affected keys immediately.

Marco Rivera: Logging/alerts to add:
- Alert if non-ops SA reads >3 secrets in 15m in any namespace -> page sec-oncall.
- Vault audit: enable JSON sink + remote syslog for retention 90d.
- KMS: enable key usage logs (decrypt/unwrap) and forward to SOC.

Sam Lee: Caveats: re-seal can change metadata apps rely on. My script will preserve app.kubernetes.io/*, redwood.com/env, and custom annotations. Also add a smoke-test that hits key routes after rollout.

Jenna Carter: After prod rotation we'll keep elevated monitoring for 72h and run an integrity check: compare secret checksums before/after and run integration test suite. If anything fails, fallback to previous release and investigate.

Priya Patel: Assignments:
- Priya: generate keypair, upload cert, create re-seal scripts + PR, update incident doc (T+1h)
- Marco: RBAC + admission annotation check PR (T+3h)
- Sam: run re-seal in staging/dev, run scans, produce checklist (T+6h)
- Jenna: KMS wrap design, helm values, prod window coordination (T+12h)

Priya Patel: I'll update INC-2026-011 with runbook and paste logs here. If anyone finds additional exposed artifacts tag me @priya.patel.

Marco Rivera: LGTM.

Sam Lee: On it. Will post scan results here.

Priya Patel: Thank you team. After the prod rotation we'll run a post-rotation audit for 72h then close INC-2026-011. :lock:
